newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to convert debt to round number of euros.
newsitem.headline: France to convert debt to round number of euros.

text.p: France has decided it will convert its stock of debt into round numbers of euros with payment of cash rebates when necessary, French Treasury head Jean Lemierre said on Tuesday.
France will hold its first auction of Treasury bills denominated in euros on January 4, 1999 in what Lemierre said could be the first in Europe.
It will hold its first auction of government bonds, or OATS, on January 7 and its first auction of medium-term BTANs on January 21, 1999, Lemierre told the annual Paris Europlace conference.
It also plans to convert its entire stock of debt into euros at the scheduled start of a single currency.
"The method decided (for conversion of the stock) is rounding with payment of a rebate," Lemierre said.
He said France was working hard to prepare for the launch of the euro and to try and win a good share of the market when the single currency is launched.
"It is clear that our aim as an issuer is to play a role as a reference in the euro bond market," Lemierre said.
